title: IAsyncEnumerable and await foreach
hook: IEnumerable cannot await between items. IAsyncEnumerable is the language’s way to pull the next SQS page or CSV chunk without buffering the whole stream.

sections.heading: await foreach is the consumer syntax
sections.prose: C# 8 introduced IAsyncEnumerable<T> and await foreach. The iterator method is async IAsyncEnumerable<T> and uses yield return. Between yields you can await I/O. The compiler generates a state machine that implements IAsyncEnumerator. Cancellation uses [EnumeratorCancellation] CancellationToken so the foreach can pass a token into the iterator. CancellationToken on the method without that attribute is easy to get wrong — the token from await foreach WithCancellation is what you want. DisposeAsync runs when the foreach exits, including on break and exceptions, which is how you close a RabbitMQ cursor or a file stream.

snippets.label: Paging SQS with await foreach
snippets.explanation: Each page is awaited. Callers see a stream of messages, not a List allocated for the whole drain.

sections.heading: When not to stream
sections.prose: If the next step needs the full CSV in memory for a sort, IAsyncEnumerable buys nothing. If you need LINQ over async sequences, System.Linq.Async (or the newer BCL async LINQ APIs as they land) is the toolkit; the in-box LINQ-to-objects operators are synchronous. Do not mix yield return with yield break after you have already committed a side effect you cannot undo unless the consumer contract is clear. For Channels (module 15) the producer/consumer is a different shape: IAsyncEnumerable is pull, ChannelReader.ReadAllAsync is also pull but backed by a thread-safe buffer.

interviewTakeaways: await foreach pulls; it does not run the producer on a new thread by itself.
Use EnumeratorCancellation so host shutdown actually stops the iterator.
Streaming pages avoids a giant List on CSV or SQS drains.
commonPitfalls: Calling .ToListAsync() on a huge import and recreating the memory problem.
Yielding after disposing the resource the next MoveNext still needs.

jsTsCorrelations.note: JS async generators (async function*) plus for await...of are the same pull-stream idea. C# yield return in async IAsyncEnumerable is the closest language twin.
